mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p1.title: Share the perimeter
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p1.body:
A regular pentagon has 5 equal sides, so each side is $30 \div 5 = 6$ cm.

**Answer: (C) 6 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p1.title: Check
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p1.body:
$5 \times 6 = 30$ ✓. (With 5 cm sides the perimeter would only be 25 cm.)

**Answer: (C) 6 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p2.title: One third first
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p2.body:
Two thirds is 12, so one third is $12 \div 2 = 6$, and the whole number is $6 \times 3 = 18$.

**Answer: (D) 18**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p2.title: Check
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-p2.body:
One third of 18 is 6, so two thirds is 12 ✓.

**Answer: (D) 18**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-01.title: Count in pairs
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-01.body:
5 coins make £10, and £50 is 5 lots of £10, so $5 \times 5 = 25$ coins make £50.

**Answer: (C) 25**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-02.title: Work out each one
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-02.body:
A: $2 \times 9 = 18$. B: $2 - 9 = -7$. C: anything times 0 is 0. D: $11$. E: $2 - 0 = 2$. The greatest is 18.

**Answer: (A) $2 \times (0 + 1 + 8)$**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-02.title: Compare A and D
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-02.body:
B, C and E are clearly small. A doubles $0 + 1 + 8 = 9$, giving 18, while D only adds 2 to it, giving 11.

**Answer: (A) $2 \times (0 + 1 + 8)$**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-03.title: The last quarter
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-03.body:
After bedtime one quarter of the book is left. That quarter is the 22 pages read at breakfast plus the 35 still left: $22 + 35 = 57$ pages. The whole book is $4 \times 57 = 228$ pages.

**Answer: (E) 228**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-04.title: Count legs for each option
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-04.body:
Every option has 14 heads. Geese have 2 legs and sheep 4:
- A: $16 + 24 = 40$
- B: $12 + 32 = 44$
- C: $18 + 20 = 38$ ✓
- D: $10 + 36 = 46$
- E: $20 + 16 = 36$

**Answer: (C) 9 geese and 5 sheep**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-04.title: Start with all geese
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-04.body:
If all 14 animals were geese there would be 28 legs. There are $38 - 28 = 10$ extra legs, and each sheep has 2 more legs than a goose, so there are 5 sheep and 9 geese.

**Answer: (C) 9 geese and 5 sheep**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-05.title: Simplify both sides
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-05.body:
A: $\frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}$ (divide top and bottom by 3), and $\frac{1 \times 5}{2 \times 4} = \frac{5}{8}$ ✓.

The others fail: B gives $\frac{8}{15}$, which is less than $\frac{24}{35}$; C gives $\frac{9}{24} = \frac{3}{8}$, less than a half, but $\frac{33}{46}$ is more than a half; D gives $\frac{8}{35}$ and E gives $\frac{5}{48}$, both much less than a half, while $\frac{42}{57}$ and $\frac{51}{68}$ are more than a half.

**Answer: (A)**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-05.title: Compare with one half
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-05.body:
Every left-hand fraction is more than $\frac{1}{2}$. On the right, only A ($\frac{5}{8}$) and B ($\frac{8}{15}$) are more than a half. Checking those two: $\frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}$ ✓, but $\frac{24}{35} \ne \frac{8}{15}$ (since $24 \times 15 = 360$ and $35 \times 8 = 280$).

**Answer: (A)**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-06.title: What is left
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-06.body:
In the first 10 minutes he jabs $10 \times 6 = 60$ patients, leaving $300 - 60 = 240$. Over 20 minutes that is $240 \div 20 = 12$ per minute.

**Answer: (B) 12**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-07.title: List the multiples
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-07.body:
The multiples of 91 are 91, 182, 273, 364, 455, … The first of these that lies in one of the ranges is 455, in 401 to 460.

**Answer: (E) 401 to 460**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-07.title: Check each range
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-07.body:
91 is just past 60; 182 is past 160; 273 is past 260; 364 is past 360. But $5 \times 91 = 455$ lies between 401 and 460.

**Answer: (E) 401 to 460**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-08.title: Use the offer first
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-08.body:
The offer is cheaper per song (70p instead of 79p). Three offers would cost £10.50, too much, so he buys 2 offers: 10 songs for £7. With £3 left he can buy $300 \div 79 = 3$ more songs (costing £2.37). Total $10 + 3 = 13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-08.title: Check 14 is impossible
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-08.body:
14 songs as 2 offers plus 4 singles costs $700 + 316 = 1016$p, more than £10. With fewer offers it costs even more. So 13 is the most.

**Answer: (D) 13**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-09.title: 10 more each
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-09.body:
Each of 11, 12, …, 20 is 10 more than the matching number in 1, 2, …, 10. So the sum is $55 + 10 \times 10 = 155$.

**Answer: (C) 155**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-09.title: Pairs
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-09.body:
Pair them: $11 + 20 = 12 + 19 = \dots = 31$. There are 5 pairs, so the sum is $5 \times 31 = 155$.

**Answer: (C) 155**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-11.title: Compare two lines
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-11.body:
Beans on toast costs 40p more than egg on toast, so beans cost 40p more than egg. The items differ only if one of them is the expensive one, so beans must cost 80p and every other item 40p. Check: bacon, sausage and egg $= 3 \times 40 = 120$p ✓; toast, beans and sausage $= 40 + 80 + 40 = 160$p ✓.

**Answer: (B) Beans**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-11.title: Find the ordinary price
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-11.body:
Bacon, sausage and egg costs £1.20 for three items. If all three were ordinary, each costs 40p. Then egg on toast (80p) is two ordinary items ✓, beans on toast (£1.20) is 40p + 80p, so beans are the doubled item.

**Answer: (B) Beans**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-12.title: Follow the route
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-12.body:
Her run has six straight stages. Along the top edge and down the right side, her distance from $S$ grows (more slowly on the second stage). On the next short edge, as she turns back in towards the corner of the L, she gets a little closer to $S$, making a dip. After that the rest of the route is the mirror image of the first half, so the graph rises again and then falls back to 0. Only graph A has two peaks with a dip, rising and falling in that pattern.

**Answer: (A)**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-12.title: Rule the others out
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-12.body:
E never comes back to 0, but she returns to $S$. B and D have no dip, but she gets closer to $S$ while going round the inside corner of the L. C has straight sides with no change in steepness, but the distance grows more slowly along the second edge, as in A.

**Answer: (A)**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-13.title: Look from each direction
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-13.body:
The ornament fits a $4 \times 4 \times 4$ cube with steps cut away, and every cut-away face is parallel to a face of the cube. So looking from any of the five directions (front left, front right, back left, back right and top), you see exactly $4 \times 4 = 16$ small faces, and every outside face is seen from exactly one of these directions. Total $5 \times 16 = 80$ diamonds.

**Answer: (E) 80**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-13.title: Compare with a full cube
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-13.body:
Cutting steps out of the cube doesn't change the outside area: each face removed is replaced by a new face pointing the same way. A full $4 \times 4 \times 4$ cube has 5 faces (not counting the base) of 16 small squares each: 80.

**Answer: (E) 80**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-14.title: Inside first
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-14.body:
The factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, so $[20] = 6$. The factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, so $[18] = 6$. Then $[6 \times 6] = [36]$. The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36, so the answer is 9.

**Answer: (D) 9**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-14.title: Factor pairs of 36
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-14.body:
After finding $[20] = [18] = 6$, list factor pairs of 36: $1 \times 36$, $2 \times 18$, $3 \times 12$, $4 \times 9$, $6 \times 6$. That is $4 \times 2 + 1 = 9$ factors (6 is only counted once).

**Answer: (D) 9**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-15.title: Find the other angles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-15.body:
The marks show that each half of the top side equals the height of the rectangle, so the two corner triangles are right-angled and isosceles, with 45° angles. At each bottom corner, the 90° is split into 45° (corner triangle), $x$, and the angle $z$ next to the bottom edge.

The reflex angle is 212°, so the angle inside the bottom triangle at its top is $360° - 212° = 148°$. The bottom triangle is isosceles (marked sides), so $z = (180° - 148°) \div 2 = 16°$. Hence $x = 90° - 45° - 16° = 29°$.

**Answer: (E) 29°**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-15.title: The arrowhead
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-15.body:
Look at the "arrowhead" shape with corners at the top middle, the two bottom corners and the point marked 212°. Its angles add up to 360°. The top angle is 90° (because $180° - 45° - 45° = 90°$), the reflex angle is 212°, and each bottom corner angle is $x$. So $90 + 212 + 2x = 360$, giving $2x = 58$ and $x = 29°$.

**Answer: (E) 29°**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-16.title: Change to hours
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-16.body:
$2018 = 33 \times 60 + 38$, so 2018 minutes is 33 hours 38 minutes, i.e. 1 day 9 hours 38 minutes. One day before Wednesday midday is Tuesday midday; 9 hours 38 minutes before that is 02:22 on Tuesday.

**Answer: (B) 02:22 on Tuesday**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-16.title: Rule out by day
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-16.body:
2018 minutes is more than a day (1440 minutes) but less than two days (2880 minutes), so the time is on Tuesday, between Monday midday and Tuesday midday. Only B and C are on Tuesday. $2018 - 1440 = 578$ minutes $= 9$ h 38 min before Tuesday midday: 02:22.

**Answer: (B) 02:22 on Tuesday**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-17.title: Find the repeating block
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-17.body:
Following the diagonal rows, the pattern repeats in $3 \times 3$ blocks of tiles: each block has 1 black tile, 4 grey tiles and 4 white tiles. A large wall is made of many such blocks, so the ratio is $1 : 4 : 4$.

**Answer: (B) 1 : 4 : 4**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-18.title: Divide directly
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-18.body:
$500\,018 - 1 = 500\,017 = 7 \times 71\,431$, so 500 018 is one more than a multiple of 7. (For example, $400\,015 = 7 \times 57\,145$ is itself a multiple of 7.)

**Answer: (E) 500 018**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-19.title: 1 cm on the map
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-19.body:
18 cm stands for 450 km, so 1 cm stands for $450 \div 18 = 25$ km $= 2\,500\,000$ cm.

**Answer: (A) 1 : 2 500 000**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-20.title: Find each side length
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-20.body:
The square has side $24 \div 4 = 6$ cm. The small triangle and the hexagon share a side, and two of their sides together make up a side of the square, so they have side 3 cm. The larger triangle's side is then 6 cm, and the pentagon's side is one hexagon side plus one large-triangle side: $3 + 6 = 9$ cm.

The outside of the shape is 3 sides of the square, 2 sides of the hexagon, 4 sides of the pentagon and 1 side of the large triangle: $18 + 6 + 36 + 6 = 66$ cm.

**Answer: (E) 66 cm**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-21.title: Count fruit-eatings
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-21.body:
12 eat oranges, 8 eat apples and 6 eat pears: $12 + 8 + 6 = 26$ "fruit-eatings" among 24 children. If all 24 ate one kind only there would be just 24, so at least one child eats more than one kind. If one child eats all three fruits, that uses 3, and the other 23 children eat one kind each: $3 + 23 = 26$ ✓. So 23 is possible.

**Answer: (D) 23**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-21.title: Build it
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-21.body:
One child eats oranges, apples and pears. Then 11 more eat only oranges, 7 only apples and 5 only pears: $1 + 11 + 7 + 5 = 24$ children, with 12, 8 and 6 eating each fruit ✓. That gives $11 + 7 + 5 = 23$ eating only one kind, and 24 is impossible.

**Answer: (D) 23**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-22.title: Groups of six
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-22.body:
For each first digit there are $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ numbers. So positions 1–6 start with 3, and positions 7–12 start with 5. The numbers starting with 5 in order are 5369, 5396, 5639, … so the 7th is 5369 and the 8th is 5396.

**Answer: (C) 5396**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-23.title: Kites and triangles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-23.body:
In P the unshaded part is one kite, so each kite is $\frac{1}{5}$ of the star. In Q the unshaded part is two of the small triangles (points of the star), so each such triangle is $\frac{1}{7}$ of the star. The shaded part of R is two kites and one triangle: $\frac{2}{5} + \frac{1}{7} = \frac{14}{35} + \frac{5}{35} = \frac{19}{35}$.

**Answer: (D) $\frac{19}{35}$**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-24.title: Split along MK
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-24.body:
Cut the shaded shape along $MK$ into two triangles.
- Triangle $KXM$: base $XK = 13 \div 2 = 6.5$ cm, height $JM = 4$ cm (the right angle at $J$). Area $\frac{1}{2} \times 6.5 \times 4 = 13$ cm².
- Triangle $KYM$: base $MY = 11 \div 2 = 5.5$ cm, height $KL = 8$ cm. Area $\frac{1}{2} \times 5.5 \times 8 = 22$ cm².

Total $13 + 22 = 35$ cm².

**Answer: (C) 35 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-24.title: Halves of triangles
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-24.body:
$MK$ splits $JKLM$ into triangle $JKM$ (area $\frac{1}{2} \times 13 \times 4 = 26$) and triangle $KLM$ (area $\frac{1}{2} \times 11 \times 8 = 44$). A line from a corner to the midpoint of the opposite side halves a triangle's area, so the shaded part is $13 + 22 = 35$ cm².

**Answer: (C) 35 cm²**

mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-25.title: Worst case
mapmc-pmc-bonus-2018-25.body:
Write $5 : 4$ as $10 : 8$; then red : white : blue $= 10 : 8 : 7$, which is 25 parts. With 100 tickets, each part is 4: 40 red, 32 white, 28 blue. Half of each colour is 20, 16 and 14. You could be unlucky and pick 19 red, 15 white and 13 blue, $19 + 15 + 13 = 47$ tickets, without having half of any colour. The 48th ticket must complete half of one colour.

**Answer: (A) 48**
